recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the work group opens a new current-style issue for RDF bullet punctuation; FHIR-18463 itself does not justify changing the modern RDF narrative.
issue_request: FHIR-18463 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core technical correction asking to remove periods from the ends of bullets on the RDF page for consistency. Jira records it as auto-approved, non-substantive, and applied for STU3.
initial_application: No Jira-keyed commit for FHIR-18463 was found. Git history shows commit 7bf7397f4a965784698e0d343f8a96789cdf4942, "Additional typos (~100 more tasks)", changed source/rdf.html shortly after the issue was filed and removed terminal periods from the historical RDF bullet lists, including the "Work still needed" list.
additional_context: The current RDF page is in build scope through source/hierarchy.xml, but it has been substantially rewritten since the STU3 page referenced by the Jira URL. The old target list is gone, and current bullet items that end with punctuation are sentence-style prose rather than evidence that the old technical correction remains unapplied. Zulip and Confluence searches found no related discussion or later work-group direction changing that conclusion.
reconciliation: An empty no-change audit commit was published. No source edit was made because applying FHIR-18463 as a new broad punctuation cleanup would be optional style churn, not a necessary current-spec correction.
